He that shall be found Guilty of Cowardice in the time of engagements, shall suffer what Punishment the Captain and the Majority of the Company shall think fit.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: He that shall have the _____ to lose a Limb in time of Engagement, shall have the Sum of Six hundred pieces of Eight, and remain aboard as long as he shall think fit
Pirate code.fact: He that shall have the Misfortune to lose a Limb in time of Engagement, shall have the Sum of Six hundred pieces of Eight, and remain aboard as long as he shall think fit.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: He that sees a Sail first, shall have the best Pistol or _____ aboard of her
Pirate code.fact: He that sees a Sail first, shall have the best Pistol or Small Arm aboard of her.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: He that shall be guilty of _____ in time of Engagement shall suffer what Punishment the Captain and Majority of the Company shall think fit
Pirate code.fact: He that shall be guilty of Drunkenness in time of Engagement shall suffer what Punishment the Captain and Majority of the Company shall think fit.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: X. No snapping of _____ in the Hold
Pirate code.fact: X. No snapping of Guns in the Hold.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: Article IV's reference to no going ashore "till the ship is off the ground" suggests that the _____ was already grounded when the articles were written, only days before Gow and his men were captured
Pirate code.fact: Article IV's reference to no going ashore "till the ship is off the ground" suggests that the Revenge was already grounded when the articles were written, only days before Gow and his men were captured.

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: Compensation is provided the _____ for the use of his ship, and the salary of the carpenter, or shipwright, who mended, careened, and rigged the vessel (the latter usually about 150 pieces of eight)
Pirate code.fact: Although he does not attribute these articles to any specific buccaneer captain, Exquemelin almost certainly sailed with Henry Morgan as a physician, and thus his account likely reflects Morgan's articles more accurately than any other privateer or buccaneer of the time. Compensation is provided the Captain for the use of his ship, and the salary of the carpenter, or shipwright, who mended, careened, and rigged the vessel (the latter usually about 150 pieces of eight).

Pirate code.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Pirate code.question: The captain’s primary duties included navigation and deciding when to engage in naval warfare, but the quartermaster was responsible for overseeing daily operations, including interpreting the _____
Pirate code.fact: The captain’s authority was not absolute, though the articles might have been influenced by his leadership style and the crew’s goals and experiences. The captain’s primary duties included navigation and deciding when to engage in naval warfare, but the quartermaster was responsible for overseeing daily operations, including interpreting the Articles.
